newsitem.title: SURINAM: Surinam's new vice-president threatens to quit.
newsitem.headline: Surinam's new vice-president threatens to quit.

text.p: Surinam's fledglng government received an early blow on Tuesday when new Vice President Pretaap Radhakishun threatened to resign over proposed cabinet members he said were corrupt.
"Their past is smeared. I don't want to become the Ali Baba of thieves," said Radhakishun, who took office on Saturday alongside new President Jules Wijdenbosch.

Radhakishun singled out Modilal Mungra, whose name has been put forward by the government's seven-party coalition for finance minister. Mungra was involved in a scandal in the late 1980s when as head of state-owned Surinam Airways he was caught trying to smuggle foreign currency out of the country.
"We want a fresh start with fresh people," Radhakishun said.
Wijdenbosch, who is backed by former military strongman Desi Bouterse, came to power after a tight run-off against former President Ronald Venetiaan.
The former Dutch colony of 400,000 has endured two military coups, seven years of dictatorship and widespread guerrilla activity in the last two decades.
